routing.reason: Security-sensitive feature on a ~400-line app: accounts, sessions, per-user task scoping, a migration, page forms, tests and README, with fully specified acceptance criteria.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow — a feature that touches the schema, API, page and docs needs the plan, checks and reviews — cost if wrong: a lighter flow would miss the security and migration reviews

Ruling: skip the product owner (frame) — the ticket already gives 9 testable criteria with exact status codes and bodies — cost if wrong: an unstated edge case (invalid JSON body, session expiry, rate limiting) is decided by the developer and caught only at the code or security review

Ruling: no PM, architect or UX — the design is small and fixed by the ticket (users and sessions tables, a user_id column on tasks, one auth helper, two forms on the existing page) — cost if wrong: the page forms may need a rework after the visual review

Ruling: security review at high effort — authentication, password hashing, token storage and per-user access (IDOR) — cost if wrong: a missed hole in an auth feature; a lower effort would save only a little
Ruling: plan at medium effort — one codebase, no squads, a lead plans the whole ticket — cost if wrong: a thinner plan, fixed at the plan gate

Ruling: acceptance criterion 7 means a new migration (never edit the shipped one) adds users and sessions tables and a nullable tasks.user_id, with legacy tasks left NULL so no user sees them; the dba step reviews it — cost if wrong: legacy tasks could leak to a user
Ruling: no squads — the project declares none — cost if wrong: none
Ruling: budget $2.00 — an M change in a small repo with every review step on — cost if wrong: the run stops for the user to raise it

first: test/accounts.test.ts(214,66): error TS2345: Argument of type '{ authorization?: undefined; } | { authorization: string; }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'Record<string, string> | undefined'.

criteria.why: createUser lowercases, validates the regex, and returns 201/400/409 with the right messages. A UNIQUE-constraint fallback covers races.
POST /api/sessions returns 201 with a token. Wrong user and wrong password both give the same 401, and a dummy scrypt equalises timing.
Auth is checked first on /api/tasks routes, with a strict Bearer regex, and returns 401 'authentication required'.
All task queries filter on user_id, so another user's task gives 404 like a missing one. Tests compare the response text.
DELETE /api/sessions removes the token hash and returns 204. Reusing the token gives 401.
scrypt with a 16-byte salt and timingSafeEqual; token is 32 randomBytes and only its SHA-256 is stored; responses carry no hashes.
The migration adds a nullable user_id, and `user_id = ?` never matches NULL. A legacy-database test covers it.
index.html has sign-in and sign-up forms and a sign-out button, and app.js sends the Bearer token. The test only checks the page with regexes.
New accounts and regression tests were added, tasks.test.ts now signs in, and the README documents accounts and authentication.

findings.what: There is no upper bound on password length beyond the 16 KB body cap, and each scrypt call is expensive. The README says there is no rate limiting. Unauthenticated sign-in and sign-up could be used to exhaust CPU.
createUser does a check-then-insert, with the scrypt in between. The UNIQUE catch handles the race, but it matches on the message text /UNIQUE/, which is brittle.

Changes outside the ticket: a 16 KB body limit with a 413 response, 405 handling, a changed 500 body, cache-control no-store headers, stricter JSON validation, and extra client-side CSS and accessibility changes. These are reasonable hardening but go beyond the ticket and change existing behaviour.

The UI criterion is tested by regexes on the served HTML and JS, including a `!innerHTML` check. This does not exercise the page behaviour. The file is also named 'regression' although it holds new-feature tests, and it duplicates the sign-out coverage in accounts.test.ts.

listTasks treats any non-empty done value as true, so ?done=banana means done. This is existing behaviour, left as is. A huge numeric id in the URL is passed through Number() with no safe-integer check.

The token is kept in sessionStorage, where any XSS can read it. This is acceptable here because the code avoids innerHTML, but it is a design trade-off. The 401 handler only applies to paths that start with /api/tasks.
The dummy-hash timing equalisation and the exported helpers are slightly more than the ticket needs, but they are small and justified by the 'same answer' requirement.

judge.summary: The diff meets every acceptance criterion with a sound design: user_id is enforced in every query, auth runs before body parsing, scrypt is used correctly, only token hashes are stored, and the tests are thorough. The weaknesses are scope creep (body limit, 405s, headers, a changed 500 body), no cap on password length against scrypt CPU abuse, and UI tests that are only regex checks.
